Geographic focus:
South-east China (Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian, Guangdong), South Africa (Northern Cape, North West, Johannesburg), United States (central-southern plains, Mississippi valley, Midwest)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
Typhoon Saudel caused severe flooding, landslides and mass evacuations across south-east China, with extreme 24-hour rainfall totals exceeding 500mm in parts of Fujian. South Africa experienced widespread thunderstorm activity with damaging winds, hail and heavy rainfall across northern and western provinces. The US central-southern plains and Mississippi valley are gripped by intense heat, with heat indices reaching 40–43°C, set to persist across the Midwest and southern states in the near term.
